unit_validation.claim: raster cell values are modelled flood depth in centimetres
unit_validation.corroboration: KSDMA's own Alappuzha district map PDFs classify the same surface as 'Flood Water Level (m)' with bands <4, 4-8, 8-12 and >12 m at data/raw/ksdma/flood/alappuzha_historical.pdf and alappuzha_rcp85.pdf. Those breaks correspond to 400, 800 and 1200 in the raster's own units, and the observed district values (0 to roughly 1300) reproduce exactly those classes under a centimetre reading.
unit_validation.caveat: The district PDFs cover Ambalapuzha taluk, not the whole district, and label the surface 'water level' rather than 'depth'. The scaling is corroborated; the exact datum is not documented in the raster package.

caveats: KSDMA rasters are modelled return-period flood depth, not observed inundation, road closure or damage.
Cells are ~90 m; depth is a cell value, not a measurement at a bridge, culvert or road edge.
A road sampled in a deep cell is exposed in the model; this does not establish that it was impassable, and no closure or repair cost is implied.
Crossing candidates are unverified geometric road/water intersections, not a bridge or culvert inventory.
PMGSY population fields and Census 2011 populations are separate sources and must not be added.
Census villages without a defensible coordinate are excluded from point exposure rather than placed arbitrarily.
No observed flood damage, maintenance cost or condition record supports a maintenance recommendation from these numbers.

outputs.pmgsy_road_depth.csv: per-road maximum sampled depth for each of the 12 return-period layers
outputs.osm_road_depth.csv: per-OSM-way maximum sampled depth for each layer
outputs.point_depth.csv: per-point sampled depth by layer (separate files per point layer)
